extracted.intended_audience: general readers; students of literature; creative writers interested in Toni Morrison's life and craft
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying the aesthetic, narrative, and thematic criteria exemplified by Toni Morrison's novels and public statements that writers might emulate (prose style, narrative technique, thematic focus, discipline, and ethical aims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose precision and speech fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft prose that is highly precise and faithful to speech while achieving poetic intensity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: John Leonard praised Morrison's writing as "a prose so precise, so faithful to speech and so charged with pain and wonder that the novel becomes poetry." Aim for language that echoes spoken rhythms but attains lyrical force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the harsh consequences of racism and the Black American experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Center themes that explore racism's effects and the Black American historical and contemporary experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Morrison's works are repeatedly noted for "addressing the harsh consequences of racism in the United States and the Black American experience." Treat racial history and its human consequences as substantive material, not background color.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate multiple modes (history, folklore, nightmare, music, sociology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Blend genres and modes—history, folklore, dream/nightmare elements, music, and social analysis—within fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As noted of The Bluest Eye, a strong work can be simultaneously "history, sociology, folklore, nightmare and music." Use these modes to enrich texture and thematic depth rather than as mere ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth and longevity: write to be lingered over
rubrics_metrics.description: Compose stories intended for slow reading and revisiting, with layered characters and contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Morrison sought to create stories "which could be lingered over and relished, not 'consumed and gobbled as fast food'" and ensured "these stories and their characters had a strong historical and cultural base." Prioritize density and re-readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shifting narration and postmodern re-vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Use shifting points of view, non-linear time, and re-visionist appropriation of myth/folklore to unsettle dominant narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics identify Morrison with "postmodern feminism" and praise her "shifting narration" and re-visionist use of myth and folklore to alter Euro-American dichotomies. Employ narrative architecture deliberately to contest received histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write without the white gaze
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid centering or pandering to a white perspective; write from autonomous Black subjectivities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Morrison stated she wanted to write "without the gaze, without the white gaze," making African-American culture and people the universe of her work. Resist writing that privileges validation through whiteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination over autobiographical smallness
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor imaginative invention rather than confessional focus on one's own mundane life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Morrison told her students, "I don't want to hear about your little life, OK?" — encouraging invention and the creation of distinct worlds rather than narrow autobiography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language as craft and measure of life
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat language itself as central—the tool and measure of human life and artistic purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Morrison's aphorism from her Nobel acceptance, "We die. ... But we do language. That may be the measure of our lives," implies rigorous attention to diction, rhythm, and the ethical power of words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine and disciplined practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain disciplined writing habits and persistence as part of craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biographical detail: Morrison got up at 4 a.m. to write while raising children. Use daily routine and persistence to sustain serious creative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particularized world-building to achieve universality
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell highly particularized, localized stories that nonetheless illuminate universal human concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In her Nobel lecture Morrison urged writers to "tell us your particularized world." Specificity of place, voice, and cultural detail can produce works with broad resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reclaiming identity: repossess, re-name, re-own
rubrics_metrics.description: Use fiction as a means of cultural and political reclamation—repossessing and re-naming marginalized identities and histories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Morrison described Black women writers as writing to "repossess, re-name, re-own." Craft can have explicit aims of restoring language and agency to silenced people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguity and openness of ending
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow endings and meanings to remain open to reinterpretation and revisitation rather than offering closed resolutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Morrison preferred "leaving the endings open for reinterpretation, revisitation, a little ambiguity," enabling readers to continue engaging with the text after finishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground fiction in historical research
rubrics_metrics.description: Base fictional narratives on historical incidents and archival research when appropriate to deepen authenticity and moral weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beloved was inspired by the true story of Margaret Garner, discovered during Morrison's compilation of The Black Book. Using historical sources can anchor magical or fictional elements in concrete pasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use supernatural/genre elements metaphorically and purposefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ supernatural, ghostly, or genre conventions to explore psychological, social, or historical truths rather than for mere spectacle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics note Beloved's ghost is not genre fluff: the supernatural is used to explore deeper issues and justify non-linear structure. Ensure genre devices serve thematic and structural purposes.
